description: Export full metadata records for samples and their related lineage. This endpoint retrieves complete metadata for the requested samples plus all parent and child samples, including every recorded attribute. It supports JSON output grouped by sample type by default, or Excel (.xlsx) export when output_format is set to “excel,” and include_tree false returns only the named samples. Any logged-in user may call it; rows are limited to the caller's projects. Use this endpoint whenever the user asks to retrieve, export, download, or analyze sample data, even if they refer to “all associated” or “derived” samples. Example queries include: “Retrieve all associated samples and their metadata for NHP-220630FLY-1-PUB,” “Export full metadata for these samples as JSON,” “Download an Excel spreadsheet with data for samples 12345 and 67890,” “Get all sample data for these three monkeys,” and “Export tissue and cell sample metadata derived from this patient.”

Retrieve all assays (experimental procedures) you have access to. Returns assay titles, types, technologies used, and IDs for linked studies, samples, and data files. Examples: 'Show me all available assays'; 'What experimental procedures have been run on the primate samples?'

Retrieve all investigations (research topics or themes) you have access to. Returns investigation titles, descriptions, and IDs for their parent projects and child studies. Examples: 'Show me all ongoing investigations'; 'What research topics are being studied in the primate project?'

Retrieve all registered researchers and users in the system. Returns names, email addresses, institutions, and IDs for their associated projects, studies, and contributions. Examples: 'Show me all researchers in the system'; 'Who are the scientists working on primate studies?'

Retrieve all research projects you have access to. Returns project titles, descriptions, and IDs for related team members, investigations, studies, assays, and data files. Examples: 'Show me all projects I am part of'; 'What research projects are studying water toxicity?'

Retrieve all sample type definitions available in the system. Returns a list of sample type schemas including their titles, descriptions, and attribute configurations for categories like tissue samples, cell lines, animals, imaging data, and sequencing data. Examples: 'What types of samples can I register?'; 'Show me all available sample categories'

Search, filter and count samples from the sample graph, inside the caller's projects: the server adds the caller's project scope (a superuser sees every project), so a non-superuser never sees or counts a sample of another project. The body is a search over sample metadata: sampletype (a sample type code, or a list of codes), filter_searchText (a term or phrase matched against metadata values, or "" when the other fields carry the search), filter_matchType (PARTIAL or EXACT), and optional extensions. extensions.where is a list of conditions {sample_type, attribute (the exact attribute title), op, value} on one sample type, with op one of =, <>, <, <=, >, >=, IN, CONTAINS, NOT CONTAINS, STARTS WITH, IS TRUE, IS FALSE (the last two take no value; numbers and dates compare as values). extensions.query is search text with upper-case AND, OR and NOT, parentheses, and a [TYPE] tag on a term to hold it to one sample type; OR on one level with AND or NOT needs parentheses. extensions.lineage {direction: ancestor, descendant or either, sample_type, max_hops from 1 to 12, default 4} keeps a sample only when a sample of that type lies within max_hops derivation steps, and every sample on that path is in the caller's projects. page and page_size (default 100, max 1000) are query parameters. Returns total, the graph's count of every match, and rows, one page of full sample records read from the database; a page can hold fewer rows than expected when the graph still holds a sample the database no longer has. Use it for sample questions when not using the graph op, and whenever a graph query was refused for its project scope. Examples: 'How many tissue samples have PercentNecrosis of at least 40?'; 'Mouse samples treated with NDMA that are not female'; 'Chemical samples with an NMR data sample derived from them'.

Retrieve all standard operating procedures (protocols) you have access to. Returns protocol titles, descriptions, associated projects, and file attachment metadata. Examples: 'Show me all available protocols'; 'What procedures are documented for sample collection?'
